agree.reason: The matched-gift math and the honest 26-of-61 framing are persuasive, but a reader still sore about Eastside gets a brief apology and a pivot instead of a reason to trust the school again, so many will stay unmoved.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the false 'every child guaranteed' claim and the 26-child figure is correct, but 'many of you told us how much that hurt' inflates 'a few angry notes', and 'any amount counts double' ignores the $15,000 cap.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out $85→$170, $575 per matched child and 26 children from a full match, but never states the $70,150 needed for all 61, and it skips the sobering gap between last year's $1,240 and the $15,000 needed to unlock the match.

right_comparison.reason: It never says what happens to the waiting children, or to unclaimed match money, if the reader does nothing, so giving is never set against a concrete alternative.

qualification.reason: The match is tied to a number and a date ($15,000, December 31), and the email says plainly that it won't reach all 61, though it doesn't say what is lost if the match goes unmet.

objections.reason: The Eastside grievance is named and validated, but nothing explains the closure or says what has changed, and 'I'm asking you to look at who is waiting now' can read as dismissive to the very readers who resist most, including one who forwards emails with comments.

fit.reason: It is a short year-end appeal of roughly 250 words with a subject line, a call-to-action button and a P.S., signed by the executive director as asked.
